correctness.rationale: For positive rates with beta=a1+b2<delta=b1+a2, first-principles transition marking yields exponential eigenfunction exp(theta x+u h), u=log((b1 e^theta+a2)/delta). At h=0 and h>0 its generator eigenvalue is lambda=(b1b2/delta)(e^theta-1)+(a1a2/delta)(e^-theta-1), since tilted death intensity is delta. Uniform Poisson jump domination makes the exponential martingale true. Under the tilted law, gap is M/M/1 with birth beta_theta=BC/delta, death delta; in I, stationary geometric tail integrates e^-u h when B<delta, giving prefactor exp(u h0)(delta-beta_theta)/(delta-B). An exponential Lyapunov bound supplies uniform integrability for u<0. Tilted ergodic theorem and bounded-jump martingale strong law supply local speed lambda prime(theta), and inverse-density bounds give the local LD exponent for x in lambda prime(I). Independently checked tilt eigenidentities in exact rational z=e^theta for three stable parameter choices at three z each; inspected verify.py and explicitly separated finite comparisons from infinite-time proof.
